correctness.rationale: For all rooted full binary five-tip strictly positive-edge ultrametric trees under uniform size-k sampling, rooted Faith PD is a finite branch-indicator sum. Exact subset enumeration gives the two 2+3 variance-difference quadratics; the two possible 1+4 shapes yield positive-coefficient formulas for 100(V3−V2) and 25(V3−V2), proving impossibility there for all permitted edge lengths. The 2+3 witness H=10,a=1,b=6,c=7 satisfies 0<a<H, 0<b<c<H and has V=(0,789/100,171/25,174/25,0), proving sharpness. With at most four tips there cannot be two non-adjacent strict interior peaks. Rational checker compares four algebraic coefficient identities and reconstructs five exact subset variance profiles. Finite enumerations on the fixed five-tip shapes are exhaustive because there are precisely three shapes; computations are not claimed to prove larger-tree cases.

originality.rationale: The 2012 Nipperess–Matsen paper supplies the general exact rooted Faith-PD rarefaction variance identity, which is acknowledged as known. This result instead classifies the first possible double-modal variance sequence by rooted ultrametric tree shape: both 1+4 topologies are excluded by strictly positive coefficient identities, while the 2+3 topology admits precisely the derived pair of strict quadratic inequalities, witnessed by an all-positive length integer tree. Material comparison with the primary full-text source and related rarefaction/ecological distributions found no explicitly dominating shape-and-modality classification. A specialized prior equivalence remains a real risk, not a claim of proven novelty.
residual_risks: A specialized phylogenetic-diversity variance shape table or an overlooked supplementary proof could already imply the 5-tip classification despite absence in inspected papers.
A broad unlocated combinatorial inequality for tree rarefaction variances may cover both positive coefficient formulas after substitution.
Search results cannot establish global unpublished independence or exhaustive novelty.

value.rationale: Rooted phylogenetic diversity is a standard ecological summary; uncertainty across sample depths matters in biodiversity rarefaction. A common informal expectation is one variance peak; the theorem exhibits two despite ultrametric molecular-clock branch lengths, proves minimal taxon count five, and identifies which natural root split and exact age relations permit it. This is a complete structural classification for a first nontrivial taxon count with a mathematically motivated invariant, not an arbitrary finite checksum or the known general variance formula. It does not claim an empirical monitoring-design improvement or a theorem on larger trees.
